correctness.rationale: A line can be adjacent only to a hyperplane, so any total dominating set must contain hyperplanes whose intersection has no nonzero vector; codimension subadditivity forces at least \(d\) of them. A dual basis gives \(d\) hyperplanes with trivial intersection, and they form a clique that dominates every nonzero proper subspace. Equality forces exactly such a hyperplane set. Passing from ordered dual bases to unordered projective lines gives the stated count. The clique has a perfect matching in even rank; in odd rank one extra hyperplane gives the sharp even-size paired witness. Independent \(\mathbb F_2\) enumeration reproduced the rank-two and rank-three minima and counts.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification on the canonical linear family of join graphs. It recovers rank from total domination, characterizes and enumerates all minima as projective dual bases, and isolates the exact parity surcharge for paired domination.
residual_risks: A later or poorly indexed note could contain the same projective-geometry formulation; no such source was located in the targeted searches.

final_claim: For \(G\cong C_p^d\), \(d\ge2\), the join graph has \(\gamma_t=d\); its minimum total dominating sets are exactly the \(d\) hyperplanes with trivial intersection, counted by \(|GL(d,p)|/((p-1)^d d!)\), and \(\gamma_{pr}=d\) for even \(d\) and \(d+1\) for odd \(d\).
limitations: Minimum paired dominating sets are not enumerated in odd rank.
